info.title: TenkaCloud Simulator API
info.description: Independent local cloud simulator. AWS is the first provider, with documented S3, Systems Manager Parameter Store, SQS, Lambda, CloudFormation and IAM role subsets. No real infrastructure is created. This document describes only implemented operations. S3 wire APIs retain their XML formats; Native IAM roles use Query/XML; legacy identity control remains a separate JSON API. Native role ownership blocks legacy PUT/DELETE with HTTP409. Use unsigned requests or dummy TCSIM SDK credentials. Default principal simulator-admin has full sandbox access. IAM Query routing uses X-Simulator-Service: iam (or the dummy SDK signature scope), root POST and Version2010-05-08. Nine bounded role/inline-policy operations are implemented; no STS, managed policies, Conditions or non-root paths. Native Lambda roles must trust lambda.amazonaws.com. Legacy CFN/local identity roles retain their prior metadata-only trust semantics. For IAM exercises send x-simulator-principal. SQLite is ephemeral by default; --state persists it. See /_simulator/v1/capabilities for limits and deviations. Lambda supports a bounded Python 3.12 ZIP subset through the native REST paths below. Host Python is not required. A limited saved-role local SSM/S3 function SDK is supported; arbitrary network/HTTP and Function URLs remain unsupported. CloudFormation supports inline Python AWS::Lambda::Function with index.handler, existing local role, Ref/Arn and explicit DependsOn. Caller requires Lambda Create/DeleteFunction and iam:PassRole; tagged creation also requires lambda:TagResource. Only the declared saved-role SSM/S3 capability bridge is available, with no arbitrary network or managed-policy grants. Function SDK limits: S3 object body32KiB, native response48KiB before capability encoding, message64KiB,128calls and1MiB request/response aggregate. Oversized native SSM or S3 responses return EntityTooLarge without a partial successful result. API Gateway REST APIs support an explicit REGIONAL/NONE/Lambda AWS_PROXY subset. Deployments freeze resources and integrations; stages refer to a deployment. No public endpoint or real AWS is created. Local invocation requires the host access token/session and a bounded Lambda apigateway.amazonaws.com resource permission with a matching local execute-api SourceArn. Responses are non-executing downloads, with protected cookie/navigation/CORS/CSP headers removed. Active browser app hosting, WAF, custom domains, authorizers, binary media, API keys, caching, stage editing and full WP grading remain unsupported.

post.summary: SSM/SQS JSON, CloudFormation Query, or IAM Query operation
post.description: Native regional root endpoint. SQS: X-Amz-Target AmazonSQS.CreateQueue, ListQueues, GetQueueUrl, DeleteQueue, SendMessage, ReceiveMessage, DeleteMessage, ChangeMessageVisibility, GetQueueAttributes (JSON 1.0, Standard queues only; FIFO, Query protocol, batch operations and dead-letter redrive are unsupported). SSM: X-Amz-Target AmazonSSM.PutParameter, GetParameter, GetParameters, GetParametersByPath, DescribeParameters, DeleteParameter. CloudFormation: CreateStack, DescribeStacks, DeleteStack; only S3 buckets, SSM parameters, inline Python Lambda functions and one inline IAM identity policy per role. Unsupported options fail. Real credentials and session tokens are rejected. Create/DeleteStack also require the caller to allow the underlying S3/SSM/IAM/Lambda actions; CAPABILITY_IAM grants no permissions. No service RoleArn or general CloudFormation lifecycle is supported. IAM is global: send X-Simulator-Service: iam, Version2010-05-08 and one of CreateRole/GetRole/ListRoles/DeleteRole/PutRolePolicy/GetRolePolicy/DeleteRolePolicy/ListRolePolicies/UpdateAssumeRolePolicy. Policy documents are JSON strings; successful IAM XML returns them RFC3986 URL-encoded. Native role names use the local alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen subset,1–64; inline policy names1–128 AWS characters. Trust and aggregate policies32KiB, at most10 inline policies/100 statements,1000 active+retired name claims. Deleted role names cannot be adopted by legacy identity writes. No managed grants or session issuance.

put.description: Requires s3:CreateBucket on the bucket ARN. Empty body creates in us-east-1. Other supported regions require LocationConstraint. Bucket subresources: use ?versioning for Get/PutBucketVersioning; ?publicAccessBlock for Get/Put/DeletePublicAccessBlock; ?versions for GET ListObjectVersions. Do not combine subresources or send list-type with them. Versioning Status is Enabled/Suspended; MFA Delete is unsupported. Public access block stores the four bucket-level booleans; public ACLs/policies remain unsupported. Bucket tags use ?tagging. GET requires s3:GetBucketTagging; PUT/DELETE require s3:PutBucketTagging. User-defined metadata only, no ABAC/billing/system tags. An empty replacement removes the set; an absent set returns NoSuchTagSet.

post.summary: Manage IAM roles and inline policies
post.description: Global native IAM Query/XML on the existing AWS provider alias. This is the same role/inline-policy SQLite state used by native SDKs, Lambda and the console. The IAM service header below is required and prefilled. Select one of the nine verified request examples. Policies are JSON strings; response policy documents are RFC3986 URL encoded. Only root-path local role names and explicit service-principal trust are supported. No STS, managed policies, advanced Conditions, users or federation. Default roles grant no service permissions. Delete inline policies before DeleteRole. Local tokens remain mandatory in the CLI. See capabilities for limits and docs/iam.md for the bounded contract.
